chunks: And it is narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That a man asked him about the sacrificial offering, so he said:
"It is obligatory upon every Muslim, except one who does not have the means."
Then the questioner said to him: "What do you hold regarding the dependents?"
He said: "If you wish, you may do it, and if you wish, you may not do it. But as for you, do not leave it."

key_terms.لَا تَدَعْهُ: do not abandon it or leave it undone
key_terms.لَمْ يَجِدْ: did not have the means or ability to afford it
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim subject to the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْأَضْحَى: the sacrificial offering performed on Eid al-Aḍḥā

ai.seo_question: Is the Eid sacrificial offering obligatory for every Muslim and for one's dependents?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the sacrificial offering is obligatory upon every Muslim who has the means to perform it. It also distinguishes between the personal obligation of the individual and offering on behalf of one's dependents, which is left optional.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3044 - It is narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abu ʿAbdillah (as), that a man asked him about the sacrifice (udhiyya).
Imam (as) replied: "It is obligatory upon every Muslim except for one who cannot afford it."
The questioner then asked: "What do you say regarding the dependents?"
Imam (as) said: "If you wish, you may perform it for them, and if you wish, you may not. However, as for you, do not neglect it."
